src.q: Each capsule contains as the active ingredient, cefalexin monohydrate equivalent to 250 mg of cefalexin base.

formulations.label: Granules for oral suspension
formulations.note: Contains sucrose (about 2.97 g per 5 mL) and the colour Allura Red AC (E129).

src.q: each 5 ml of reconstituted suspension contains as the active ingredient, cefalexin monohydrate equivalent to 250 mg of cefalexin base
Contains 2.972 g of Sucrose per 5 ml after reconstitution. Also contains Allura Red AC (E129).

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Infections due to susceptible organisms: respiratory tract infections, otitis media, skin and soft tissue infections, bone and joint infections, genito-urinary tract infections (including acute prostatitis), dental infections.

src.q: Cefalexin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections due to susceptible micro-organisms
Respiratory tract infections Otitis media Skin and soft tissue infections Bone and joint infections Genito-urinary tract infections, including acute prostatitis Dental infections

restrictions.note: No specialist-only, shared-care or brand-specific prescribing restriction found in the cefalexin capsule and suspension SmPCs.

items.t: Adults: 1 to 4 g daily in divided doses; most infections respond to 500 mg every 8 hours. If more than 4 g daily is needed, consider parenteral cephalosporins.

src.q: The adult dosage ranges from 1-4g daily in divided doses; most infections will respond to a dosage of 500 mg every 8 hours.
If daily doses of cefalexin greater than 4g are required, parenteral cephalosporins, in appropriate doses, should be considered.

items.t: Skin and soft tissue infections, streptococcal pharyngitis, mild uncomplicated UTI: usually 250 mg every 6 hours or 500 mg every 12 hours. More severe infections may need larger doses.

src.q: For skin and soft tissue infections, streptococcal pharyngitis and mild, uncomplicated urinary tract infections, the usual dosage is 250 mg every 6 hours, or 500 mg every 12 hours.

items.t: Beta-haemolytic streptococcal infections: treat for at least 10 days.

src.q: In the treatment of beta-haemolytic streptococcal infections, a therapeutic dose should be administered for at least 10 days.

items.t: Elderly and renal impairment: as for adults, but reduce the dose if renal function is markedly impaired.

src.q: The elderly and patients with impaired renal function As for adults. Reduce dosage if renal function is markedly impaired

items.t: Children: usually 25 to 50 mg/kg/day in divided doses. For skin and soft tissue infections, streptococcal pharyngitis and mild uncomplicated UTI the daily dose may be divided every 12 hours.

src.q: The usual recommended daily dosage for children is 25-50 mg/kg (10-20 mg/lb) in divided doses.
the total daily dose may be divided and administered every 12 hours

items.t: Suggested schedule for most infections: under 5 years 125 mg every 8 hours; 5 years and over 250 mg every 8 hours. In severe infections the dose may be doubled.

src.q: Children under 5 years: 125 mg every 8 hours. Children 5 years and over: 250 mg every 8 hours. In severe infections, the dosage may be doubled.

items.t: Otitis media: 75 to 100 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses.

src.q: In the therapy of otitis media, clinical studies have shown that a dosage of 75 to 100 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses is required.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to cefalexin or any excipient; known allergy to the cephalosporin group.

src.q: Cefalexin is contraindicated in patients with known allergy to the cephalosporin group of antibiotics.

items.t: Before starting, try to find out about previous hypersensitivity to cephalosporins, penicillins or other drugs. Give cautiously to penicillin-sensitive patients (partial cross-allergenicity; severe reactions including anaphylaxis to both). Stop if an allergic reaction occurs.

src.q: every effort should be made to determine whether the patient has had previous hypersensitivity reactions to the cephalosporins, penicillins or other drugs
Cefalexin should be given cautiously to penicillin-sensitive patients.
If an allergic reaction to cefalexin occurs, the drug should be discontinued

items.t: Markedly impaired renal function: use with caution; safe dose may be lower. On dialysis, the daily dose should not exceed 500 mg.

src.q: Cefalexin should be administered with caution in the presence of markedly impaired renal function.
If dialysis is required for renal failure, the daily dose of cefalexin should not exceed 500mg.

items.t: Neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures): higher risk in the elderly, severe renal impairment or CNS disorders. Consider stopping if suspected.

src.q: Elderly patients, patients with severe renal impairment or central nervous system disorders are particularly at risk.
If cefalexin associated neurotoxicity is suspected, discontinuation of cefalexin should be considered.

items.t: Nephrotoxicity risk may increase with aminoglycosides, other cephalosporins, or furosemide and similar potent diuretics.

src.q: Concurrent administration with certain other drug substances, such as aminoglycosides, other cephalosporins, or furosemide, (frusemide) and similar potent diuretics, may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity.

items.t: AGEP: advise patients of the signs and monitor closely; withdraw immediately if it appears (mostly in the first week).

src.q: If signs and symptoms suggestive of these reactions appear, cefalexin should be withdrawn immediately and an alternative treatment considered.

items.t: Consider pseudomembranous colitis in patients with diarrhoea; it can be life-threatening. Prolonged use may cause overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms.

src.q: It is important, therefore, to consider its diagnosis in patients who develop diarrhoea in association with the use of antibiotics.
Prolonged use of cefalexin may result in the overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms.

items.t: Suspension contains sucrose: patients with hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it. E129 may cause allergic reactions.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.
Also contains Allura Red AC (E129), which may cause allergic reactions.

items.t: Lab tests: positive direct Coombs test (including in newborns of treated mothers); false positive urine glucose with copper-reduction tests.

src.q: Positive direct Coombs' tests have been reported during treatment with the cephalosporin antibiotics.
A false positive reaction for glucose in the urine may occur with Benedict's or Fehling's solutions or with copper sulphate test tablets.

items.t: Furosemide and similar potent diuretics, aminoglycosides, other cephalosporins: may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity.

src.q: Concurrent administration with certain other drug substances, such as aminoglycosides, other cephalosporins, or furosemide, (frusemide) and similar potent diuretics, may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity.

items.t: Metformin: single-dose study showed raised metformin levels (Cmax +34%, AUC +24%); clinical significance unclear and no lactic acidosis reported.

src.q: plasma metformin Cmax and AUC increased by an average of 34% and 24%, respectively
The clinical significance of this study is unclear

items.t: Probenecid inhibits renal excretion of cefalexin.

src.q: As with other beta-lactam drugs, renal excretion of cephalexin is inhibited by probenecid.

items.t: Markedly impaired renal function: reduce dose and use with caution; safe dose may be lower than usual. The SmPC gives no CrCl/eGFR threshold.

src.q: Reduce dosage if renal function is markedly impaired
Careful clinical and laboratory studies should be made because safe dosage may be lower than that usually recommended.

items.t: Dialysis: daily dose should not exceed 500 mg.

src.q: If dialysis is required for renal failure, the daily dose of cefalexin should not exceed 500mg.

hepatic.note: The cefalexin capsule and suspension SmPCs give no hepatic impairment advice (transient hepatitis and cholestatic jaundice are listed only as rare adverse effects).

items.t: SmPC: no evidence of teratogenicity, but exercise caution when prescribing in pregnancy.

src.q: Although laboratory and clinical studies have shown no evidence of teratogenicity, caution should be exercised when prescribing for the pregnant patient.

items.t: BUMPS (UKTIS, cephalosporins incl. cefalexin): most studies have not shown harm; no extra monitoring for major birth defects needed.

src.q: Most studies of pregnant women taking a cephalosporin have not shown that it harms the baby.
No extra monitoring for major birth defects is required following use of a cephalosporin.

items.t: SmPC: present in milk up to 8 hours after a dose. Use with caution: risk of candidiasis and CNS toxicity in the neonate, and theoretical later sensitisation.

src.q: Caution should be exercised when cefalexin is administered to a nursing woman, since the neonate is presented with the risk of candidiasis and CNS toxicity due to immaturity of the blood-brain barrier.

reproductive.note: The cefalexin capsule and suspension SmPCs give no fertility or contraception information.

items.t: Diarrhoea is the most frequent side effect (rarely severe enough to stop). Dyspepsia and abdominal pain also occur; nausea and vomiting are rare. The SmPC gives no other frequencies.

src.q: The most frequent side-effect has been diarrhoea. It was very rarely severe enough to warrant cessation of therapy.
Nausea and vomiting have been reported rarely.

items.t: Allergic rash, urticaria; genital and anal pruritus, genital candidiasis, vaginitis, dizziness, headache.

src.q: Allergic reactions have been observed in the form of rash, urticaria, angioedema
These have included genital and anal pruritus, genital candidiasis, vaginitis and vaginal discharge, dizziness, fatigue, headache

items.t: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, erythema multiforme, SJS, TEN: stop cefalexin and treat.

src.q: rarely erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
Anaphylaxis has also been reported.

items.t: AGEP: withdraw immediately.

src.q: Acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) has been reported in association with cefalexin treatment.

items.t: Pseudomembranous colitis (mild to life-threatening), haemolytic anaemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, reversible interstitial nephritis, convulsions/encephalopathy (mostly with renal impairment and excessive doses).

src.q: Such colitis may range in severity from mild to life-threatening.
Eosinophilia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and haemolytic anaemia have been reported.
Most cases occurred in patients with renal impairment who received doses that exceeded the recommended dose

items.t: Before starting: ask about previous reactions to cephalosporins, penicillins or other drugs.

src.q: every effort should be made to determine whether the patient has had previous hypersensitivity reactions to the cephalosporins, penicillins or other drugs

items.t: Markedly impaired renal function: careful clinical and laboratory monitoring. Prolonged use: observe for superinfection. Monitor closely for skin reactions.

src.q: Careful clinical and laboratory studies should be made because safe dosage may be lower than that usually recommended.
Careful observation of the patient is essential.

items.t: Stop if an allergic reaction or AGEP occurs; consider stopping if neurotoxicity is suspected.

src.q: If an allergic reaction to cefalexin occurs, the drug should be discontinued
If cefalexin associated neurotoxicity is suspected, discontinuation of cefalexin should be considered.

items.t: Oral use.

src.q: Method of administration For oral use.

items.t: Suspension: tap the bottle to loosen the granules, add 60 mL water in two portions, shaking after each. Shake well before use. Store in a refrigerator (2 to 8 °C) after reconstitution and use within 10 days.

src.q: add a total of 60 ml water in two portions, shaking after each addition until suspended
After reconstitution: to be used within 10 days
After reconstitution, the suspension should be stored in a refrigerator

items.t: Report rash, skin pustules or allergy symptoms straight away (AGEP mostly occurs in the first week).

src.q: At the time of prescription patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions.

items.t: Report diarrhoea during or after the course.

src.q: Symptoms of pseudomembranous colitis may appear either during or after antibiotic treatment.

rules.action: Give cautiously; find out about the previous reaction first; stop if an allergic reaction occurs. The SmPC does not distinguish reaction types.

src.q: Cefalexin should be given cautiously to penicillin-sensitive patients.
There is some clinical and laboratory evidence of partial cross-allergenicity of the penicillins and cephalosporins.
